authority_map.resolution: Allowed within the workspace; no external systems or destructive git operations are required.
authority_map.scope: Create a new session-hub package and governed planning artifacts only.

constraints: Keep the implementation isolated to a new session-hub package.
Use plain HTTP + JSON request/response contracts and a --service-url based client flow.
Preserve a minimal operator surface: serve, connect, send, read.

decomposition_policy.packetization: Use one implementation packet and one validation packet.

definition_of_done.criterion: Agents can connect to the same session and exchange persisted messages through the shared service using only session id, agent id, and service URL.
Automated tests cover direct service usage and CLI flows with persisted local client state.
The service remains minimal and explicit about having no built-in auth so callers do not assume protected transport or identity verification.
Human-readable CLI output and JSON output let operators confirm the active session, sender, and message history.
The new package is isolated enough that rollback is a bounded deletion/revert of session-hub files only.

dependencies: Node.js >= 20 for fetch and node:test support

integration_map.touchpoint: Shared HTTP session service and file-backed persistence.
CLI local client-state resolution against the remote service URL.

ambiguity_classification.statement: The network layer is assumed to be provided externally by Tailscale; the package only needs to be Tailscale-reachable by host and port.

non_goals: Do not add project coordination, assignments, inboxes, briefs, derivation logic, or task state machines.
Do not add authentication, Tailscale APIs, or tunnel orchestration in this iteration.
Do not retrofit the Artifact Loop coordination model into this separate package.
intent_contract.objective: Create a file-backed HTTP service and CLI that support session connect, send, and read flows using a shared service URL.
success_criteria: A service can create or update a session and persist messages under sessions/<id>.json and messages/<session-id>/*.json.
CLI clients can connect to a session with an agent id, persist that local client session state, and then send and read messages without retyping the session on every command.
End-to-end tests prove a remote client can connect, send, and read through the HTTP service.

non_goals: No transport encryption or identity layer inside the app
No websocket or realtime push transport
compiled_contract.objective: Implement a separate minimal session messaging service and CLI so agents can connect to a shared session and exchange messages over a Tailscale-reachable HTTP endpoint.
